questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English-speaking primarily and far away

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Main downsides were that it was expensive, cold, and took quite some time to prepare.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Lots. They had many employee dedicated to the first welcome days.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: All dorms very full so the only option was to stay in a hotel room with a roommate.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Only all-inclusive meal plans

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Housing is very expensive compared to what you get. The meal plans are worth it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was alright.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You do it online and they have a tool to figure out if courses selected are compatible. There are a few weeks start of semester to try out courses. But have some courses you are pretty sure on beforehand, otherwise its alot of stress to try out courses and fall behind.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are a few weeks start of semester to try out courses. But have some courses you are pretty sure on beforehand, otherwise its alot of stress to try out courses and fall behind.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The level was alright, comparable to UCPH. I had the joy of witnessing someone live-chatgpt during an oral exam presentation without the professor noticing: D

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Took 2 300-level courses (easy for me as an MSc student) and a 500-level one (was slightly below average in term of difficulty, compared to my other MSc courses at UCP). Also tried a 699 course, which was outrageously hard so i dropped it.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Tons of assignments, even more than Computer Science at UCPH which is already notorious for having many assignments. Be prepared for weekly assignements in all courses. Professor are cool and engaged.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
CAS CS 543	Algorithmic Techniques for Taming Big Data
CAS CS 391 T1	Algorithms to live by
CAS CS 392 M1	Rust, in Practice and in Theory

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All 3 of these were actually pretty good. Check out Sublinear Algorithms if you want a real challenge ;)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The Housing and mealplan costs were not unexpected, but i didnt realize how expensive it was before i was there.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing and Mealplans more expensive than i thought. Insurance  and language test (duolingo) wasnt too bad.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I joined powerlifting and yoga, and it was very good and they have ample opportunity to join lots of different "exercise courses"

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lots lots lots

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to free concerts at Berklee. They have some amazingly talented people there, and lots of free/ cheap concerts.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: My best experiences were in NYC, at Monster Jam, Berklee, the museums (Particular Harvard and The Met and AMNH.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very tough to get used to no one holding the door for you. But otherwise fine.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Good luck! :D I found more luck with the other exchange students. Perhaps if you meet people who also eat at the dining halls its easier to keep in touch.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The fucking bathroom stalls wtf

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Audiences at concerts going batshit crazy

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go to Berklee for music, Pick easy courses and chill, bring clothes and attitude for winter.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It seems there are way more danish exchange students during the autumn, thats atleasat what i heard. in particular. from cbs.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Setting PRs in my first every powerlifting meet.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The first month where the weather was horrible and i felt homesick and like i was wasting money.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: BU is short for Boston University, but really it is short for BUSINESS. These guys are making moneyyyyyy. Its so expensive. Be prepared to apply for lots of grants, and in case you dont get any, you need about 100k DKK saved up:)) Also note that you dont have to pay the majority of the expenses before end of semester.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
